findings: Velocity check uses position delta as proxy without time normalization — if steps_per_command changes, the effective velocity threshold shifts silently. Acceptable for Phase 11 scope but worth documenting.
run_policy_on_robot accesses robot._sim (private attribute) to reuse the simulation for policy, breaking the RobotInterface abstraction. A real robot driver would need a separate sim instance.
Domain randomization mutates model parameters multiplicatively without storing originals. Calling apply_domain_randomization twice compounds the effect with no reset path.
forge_robot.py CLI compare-sim and calibrate commands access private attributes (_sim, _max_steps) directly, coupling the CLI to SimulatedRobot internals.
SimulatedRobot.send_command uses assert for connection guard — stripped under python -O. Minor since this is a simulated driver, not a real hardware path.

emergency_stop sends zero-position targets rather than holding current position. On a real Panda this would drive all joints to zero config, which may not be the safest stop behavior. Acceptable for simulation.
summary: Phase 11 implementation is well-structured and complete. All 56 tests pass (22 hardware, 12 safety, 14 sim2real). RobotInterface ABC covers all required methods, SafetyMonitor properly validates joint/velocity/workspace limits, sim2real utilities are testable and well-organized. Config loading, dataclass patterns, and CLI structure match existing project conventions. Documentation is thorough. Findings are minor design notes, none blocking.
